statement.p: Use implicit differentiation to find an equation of the tangent line to curve called the devil's curve,defined by y^{2}\mathopen{}\left(y^{2}-25\right) = x^{2}\mathopen{}\left(x^{2}-6\right), at the point \left(0,5\right).
An equation of the tangent line to the devil's curve at the given point is .
(Be sure to enter the entire equation of the line, including the "y=".

solution.p: Writing the equation as y^4 - 25 y^2 = x^4 - 6 x^2, and then differentiating implicitly with respect to x, gives (4 y^3 - 50 y) \, \frac{dy}{dx} = 4 x^3 - 12 x. If x = 0 and y = 5, then this last equation becomes 250 \, \frac{dy}{dx} = 0, \qquad \text{and so} \qquad \frac{dy}{dx} = 0, which means that the tangent line is horizontal. Therefore, the tangent line to the devil's curve at the point \left(0,5\right) is defined by the equation y = 5.
